overall: A clear, moving wordless fable whose central irony — the dodo as beloved icon but homeless animal — lands without explanation. The opening sleep / city wake-up and the closing painted-forest sleep bookend beautifully, though the middle search repeats one beat and the capture-to-park continuity loses the protagonist for a few shots.

shots.fix: Retake with the light grading down to blue dusk and the dodo's eyes closing by the final second.
shots.problem: The light stays pink-gold and the dodo only lowers its head, so the fall-asleep-and-centuries-pass transition into the city is not yet fully read.

shots.fix: Retake with a hurried scuttling gait and one clear glance back over its shoulder.
shots.problem: After the bus startle the dodo ambles calmly and looks around curiously, losing the fright and flee established in s04_startle_close.

shots.fix: Trim to about three seconds, holding only the settle and the look toward Le Pouce.
shots.problem: The dodo stands nearly motionless at the frame edge for the full shot, stalling the search montage between the gate and the souvenir wall.

shots.fix: Repainted keyframe with the dodo at believable scale on the overlook rock and the city unobstructed behind it.
shots.problem: The dodo is scaled so large against the city and racecourse below that it reads as a giant hovering over Port Louis rather than standing on a hilltop.

shots.fix: Repainted keyframe muting the umbrella canopy to the pastel range of s10_umbrellas_noticed.
shots.problem: The overhead umbrellas jump to saturated primary orange, blue and lime, breaking the muted palette and making this feel like a different location from the shots either side.

shots.fix: Trim the blurred guard's walk-through and hold on the dodo beside the open crate and gated sign.
shots.problem: The dodo is already free beside an open crate with no release beat, and the guard smears across the booth in a morphing blur, so arrival at the park does not connect to the harbour crate.

shots.fix: Trim s16_phones_flashes out entirely so the reveal cuts straight to the mural wall.
shots.problem: At under two seconds this single-dodo flash shot interrupts the many-dodos reveal before it can register and duplicates the phone motif already clear in s15_many_behind_glass.

sound: Gentle solo piano with forest birdsong in s01_forest_dawn and s02_settle_sleep establishes the 1681 calm and carries unbroken across the dissolve into traffic noise in s03_wake_city, making the time jump legible before the card is read.
The bus whoosh and traffic swell are synced to the dodo's flinch and open-beaked alarm in s04_startle_close, the one true startle sound cue in the film.

Crowd murmur builds through s10_umbrellas_noticed and s11_surrounded and cuts to the wooden lid thud in s12b_crate_closed, after which the harbour ambience in s13_crate_harbour keeps the crated journey present without showing it.

The dodo's few soft coos are well placed — a small call at the souvenir wall in s08_own_image and a longer, lower sequence as it settles by the mural in s19_press_mural and s21_sleep_again — and the score thins to near-silence under both so they read as its only voice.
strengths: The match from the mossy rock in s01_forest_dawn through s02_settle_sleep to the same rock marooned in a pavement garden bed in s03_wake_city is the film's best editorial idea: place, prop and posture carry three centuries in one cut, reinforced by the correctly placed and sparing cards.

s08_own_image delivers the theme in a single image — the living dodo studying its own mural above a row of plush dodos — with no card needed, and the generic unbranded souvenirs keep it inside the brief.

The reveal in s15_many_behind_glass, shot from the visitors' side with phone screens raised in silhouette, reframes the protagonist's loneliness as a whole species' captivity, and the card 'It was not the only one.' arrives exactly on the wide shot.

The closing movement from the peeling mural in s17_mural_wall through the slow approach in s18_walk_to_mural to the mirrored sleep in s21_sleep_again earns the end card; the dodo's design, grey-brown body and white wing patch, stays recognisably on-model throughout.
weaknesses: The search section s05_downtown_search to s09_see_mountains is five consecutive static wide shots in which the dodo mostly stands and looks, so the wandering reads as a location slideshow rather than a growing desperation.

Protagonist continuity breaks at the climax: the dodo is shut in the crate in s12b_crate_closed and crated at the harbour in s13_crate_harbour, then simply standing free in s14_park_arrival, and inside the group in s15_many_behind_glass it is impossible to tell which of the five dodos is ours.

Crowd animation is the weakest visual element: in s11_surrounded the people are faceless phone-holding cut-outs whose hands and devices flicker and morph, and the disembodied oversized hands closing the crate in s12b_crate_closed undercut the capture's gravity.

Geography is evocative but occasionally muddled — Le Pouce appears behind the canal in s07_waterfront_pouce and again dominating s09_see_mountains over Champ de Mars — so the dodo's sighting of distant mountains does not clearly motivate the move to Caudan that follows.
